claims.statement: All business data is stored in a single MySQL database (default jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/ecshopx) reached through MyBatis-Plus 3.5.16 (mybatis-plus-spring-boot3-starter, version pinned in the root pom.xml), with the MySQL JDBC driver (com.mysql:mysql-connector-j, runtime scope) declared only in ecshopx-bootstrap; ecshopx-common also declares the MyBatis-Plus starter because it hosts the shared configuration.

The JDBC URL pins characterEncoding=utf-8 and serverTimezone=Asia/Shanghai, while the Docker stacks (docker-compose.dev.yml and docker-lite/docker-compose.yml) start MySQL 8.0 with --character-set-server=utf8mb4 --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci and TZ=Asia/Shanghai; the readme's manual init creates the database as utf8mb4/utf8mb4_unicode_ci, and migrations generated by bin/make-migration emit CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci.

EcshopxApplication is the only place @MapperScan appears: basePackages cn.shopex.ecshopx.**.mapper, nameGenerator FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator, sqlSessionFactoryRef sqlSessionFactory, lazyInitialization true. Placing the scan on the main class makes MapperScannerRegistrar register MapperFactoryBean during primary-config processing, satisfying MyBatis-Plus' @ConditionalOnMissingBean(MapperFactoryBean) so its own auto mapper scanning backs off; lazyInitialization defers mapper bean creation until first use.

FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator avoids mapper bean-name collisions across the 48+ Bundles by returning the fully-qualified class name with '.' replaced by '_' for any bean definition whose class name ends in Mapper, and delegating to Spring's AnnotationBeanNameGenerator otherwise. Collisions are real: StatisticsMapper exists in both ecshopx-companys and ecshopx-data-cube, SettingMapper in ecshopx-companys and ecshopx-wsugc, and CartMapper in ecshopx-orders and ecshopx-employee-purchase.

Hard rule: a mapper interface must live in a package matching cn.shopex.ecshopx.**.mapper to be scanned; anything outside that pattern is not registered as a bean and the failure surfaces as a Spring context startup error (NoSuchBeanDefinitionException on the injecting constructor). The only deliberate exception is ecshopx-dispatch's FailedJobMapper, which sits in the bundle root package cn.shopex.ecshopx.dispatch and is wired by an explicit stub @Bean in bootstrap's DispatchBusConfig returning entity -> 1, while its real XML insert for failed_jobs lives in ecshopx-dispatch/src/main/resources/mapper/FailedJobMapper.xml — failed-job persistence is an unfinished wiring point, not a pattern to copy.

MybatisPlusCommonConfig installs exactly one MyBatis-Plus inner interceptor — PaginationInnerInterceptor(DbType.MYSQL) — which is what turns mapper.selectPage(new Page<>(page, size), wrapper) into MySQL LIMIT SQL, and registers MpMetadataAnnotationHandler as the GlobalConfig annotation handler via a MybatisPlusPropertiesCustomizer. There is no TenantLineInnerInterceptor, optimistic-lock, or block-attack interceptor.

MybatisPlusMetaHandler auto-fills audit columns for two coexisting naming conventions — createTime/updateTime as Integer Unix-epoch seconds and createdAt/updatedAt as LocalDateTime — filling all four on insert (strictInsertFill) and only updateTime/updatedAt on update (strictUpdateFill); filling triggers only on fields annotated with FieldFill.INSERT/INSERT_UPDATE. BaseEntity in ecshopx-common is the opt-in base class for the create_time/update_time convention, but most domain entities instead declare their own int created/updated columns and set them explicitly.

Domain entities in each Bundle's domain/ package use the extended metadata annotations from common/mybatis/metadata — @MpTable (meta-annotated @TableName, adding comment/indexes/uniqueIndexes), @MpId (meta-annotated @TableId), @MpField (meta-annotated @TableField, adding columnType/length/nullable/defaultValue/comment) — whose metadata was migrated from the legacy ecshopx-api Doctrine ORM.

MpMetadataAnnotationHandler implements MyBatis-Plus' AnnotationHandler so that queries for stock @TableName/@TableField/@TableId on a class or field are answered from the corresponding @MpTable/@MpField/@MpId annotation via a dynamic Proxy that synthesizes the stock annotation with the right attribute values and defaults — this is what lets the MyBatis-Plus runtime and bin/make-migration both understand entities that never mention the stock annotations directly.

bin/make-migration is domain-first schema evolution: it connects to the MySQL database from spring.datasource.* (or --db-url), reads information_schema as the from-schema, parses every ecshopx-*/src/main/java/**/domain/**/*.java with a pure-Python regex parser (reading @MpTable/@MpId/@MpField/@MpIndex, falling back to stock @TableName/@TableId/@TableField with nullability/default inferred from the Java field initializer), and emits a Flyway VyyyyMMddHHmmss__<description>.sql under ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/db/migration. Ordinary and unique indexes come only from @MpIndex; DROP statements are never emitted without --allow-drop; duplicate domain mappings for one table are resolved by a richer-wins score; generated SQL must be manually reviewed.

Tenancy is by company_id (with distributor_id as the shop dimension and distributor_id = 0 meaning the platform pool), and there is no automatic tenant filter: every query and update must be scoped explicitly with LambdaQueryWrapper/LambdaUpdateWrapper eq(Entity::getCompanyId, companyId), and hand-written XML or annotation SQL must repeat the company_id predicate itself — a forgotten predicate is a cross-tenant data leak whose only defenses are review and tests.

companyId is resolved per request by the auth interceptors (JWT claims or anonymous appid/domain resolution) and passed to services as an explicit long parameter or a small context object; controllers read it from the H5FrontAuthAttributes.H5_COMPANY_ID request attribute and throw UnauthorizedException when it cannot be resolved to a positive value. It never arrives through a thread-local the persistence layer could read on its own.

Primary-key lookups are not automatically tenant-safe: repositories add eq(companyId) even when filtering by a per-company id (getByItemIdAndCompany, deleteByItemIdsAndCompanyId, updateAuditFieldsByCompanyAndGoodsId), while selectById is reserved for globally unique keys such as the string trade_id used by payment callbacks; ItemsRepository.findByItemId is the documented rare exception that queries by item_id only, without a company filter.

The physical half of the tenant contract is indexing: nearly every @MpTable declares an @MpIndex on company_id (frequently leading a composite index such as Trade's ix_list on company_id+order_id) so the tenant predicate stays indexable; the trade table also carries a unique composite index idx_key on company_id+distributor_id+barcode in ItemsBarcode.

Legacy PHP tables stored tenant ids as strings: Trade declares companyId/distributorId/shopId/dealerId with columnType=string, so hand-written SQL comparing them must CAST(company_id AS SIGNED) before numeric comparison (as in TradeMapper.xml's Youshu statements), while newer tables like items_barcode use bigint for company_id/distributor_id.

ItemsBarcodeRepository.saveBarcode implements shop-scoped overwrite semantics with a company+shop uniqueness guard: it deletes the item's existing barcode rows with an eq(companyId).in(itemId) wrapper, then for each code counts rows matching eq(companyId).eq(distributorId).eq(barcode).ne(itemId) and throws ResourceException with message 条形码已经存在 if another SKU in the same shop owns the code, before inserting. ItemsBarcodeRepositoryShopScopedTest pins the tenant matrix: same-shop duplicate throws and never inserts, different-shop same code inserts, and distributorId 0 (the platform pool) flows through.

Payment callbacks implement idempotency as a guard on current row state: OrdersTradePaymentCallbackService.applyTradePaymentNotify first persists the raw notify payload to inital_response, then re-reads the trade and refuses to continue unless tradeState is exactly NOTPAY (otherwise throwing ResourceException 更新已处理，不需要更新), then applies a narrow LambdaUpdateWrapper keyed on eq(tradeId) setting only the payment-related columns, treats updated <= 0 as a failure (ResourceException 交易单状态更新失败), and only on SUCCESS fans out trade-finish dispatch publishers and the membercard VIP fulfillment port.

The same NOTPAY-guard/zero-rows-is-failure shape is repeated wherever an external system can redeliver an event: BsPayOrdersTradePaymentCallbackService.handlePaymentNotify, AdapayOrdersTradePaymentCallbackService, AdapayDepositTradeRechargeCallbackService.rechargeCallback (inside @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class), checking tradeStatus SUCCESS), OfflinePaymentDoCheckService, OrdersPaymentDoPaymentService, and SupplierOfflineTradeWriteService — the persistence invariant is that state-machine transitions are conditional updates gated on the previous state and a zero-affected-rows result is an error, not a no-op.

Cross-store writes follow a deliberate split: multi-write SQL flows run under @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class) (e.g. the deposit recharge callback updating the trade row and mutating the UserDeposit balance), while Redis writes are non-transactional side effects performed after the SQL work, and dispatch/SMS publication is registered via TransactionSynchronizationManager afterCommit so it only fires on successful commit; where a method must start a transaction from inside its own bean, the codebase uses a programmatic TransactionTemplate instead of a self-invoked @Transactional.

Testing MyBatis-Plus lambda wrappers without a database uses the TableInfoHelper.initTableInfo(new MapperBuilderAssistant(new MybatisConfiguration(), ""), Entity.class) @BeforeAll idiom, because lambda wrappers resolve column names from cached table metadata; the payment-callback probe tests (e.g. OrdersTradePaymentCallbackServiceNormalOrderPaySuccessPublishProbeTest) mock TradeMapper and drive applyTradePaymentNotify end-to-end this way, verifying the company_id/order_id/pay_type/trade_source_type payload of the published event.

Mapper interfaces take three shapes, all annotated @Mapper and living in a mapper package: plain extends BaseMapper<Entity> for all built-in CRUD (TradeMapper, StatisticsMapper), BaseMapper plus custom methods implemented in resources/mapper/<Mapper>.xml (ReservationRecordMapper with countConflictingReservations etc.), and annotation-only @Select interfaces with or without BaseMapper for read-only projections (WxappVipGradeOrderDetailLiteMapper, AdminOrderListSourcesLookupMapper) — with short @Select scripts on BaseMapper interfaces also accepted (CartMapper.selectCartCountSummary).

Mapper XML is discovered globally via mybatis-plus.mapper-locations=classpath*:mapper/**/*.xml with mybatis-plus.configuration.map-underscore-to-camel-case=true, so every Bundle's resources/mapper/ XML is found from the single fat jar without per-Bundle registration. The shipped default for mybatis-plus.configuration.log-impl is org.apache.ibatis.logging.stdout.StdOutImpl, i.e. every SQL statement is echoed to stdout — an operator must override this key (e.g. to NoLoggingImpl) via env vars or APP_ARGS when deploying, because nothing in the repo disables it.

The datasource and Flyway wiring that backs the mappers is carried by the shipped defaults in ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/application.properties: spring.datasource.url points at jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/ecshopx (utf-8 client encoding, serverTimezone=Asia/Shanghai), username/password ecshopx/ecshopx, driver com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver, spring.flyway.enabled=true with locations classpath:db/migration, baseline-on-migrate=true and baseline-version=0 (existing ecshopx.sql databases are baselined instead of re-running historical SQL), and encoding UTF-8. ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/application-local.properties is NOT one of these shipped defaults: it is git-ignored (.gitignore line 7) and absent from fresh checkouts (the readme's claim that the project already includes it is drift), so per-environment values arrive via environment variables or Spring Boot CLI arguments — which is exactly how both Docker compose stacks inject --spring.datasource.* and re-assert --spring.flyway.enabled=true through APP_ARGS, since Docker runs do not activate the local profile. spring.flyway.locations is classpath-wide (every Bundle ships a .gitkeep-only db/migration directory), but only ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/db/migration holds real migration SQL.
